gloss: to see through to the end; to finish completely

definitions.gloss: to see through to the end; to carry out fully; to finish completely
definitions.explanation: To do something all the way to completion without giving up partway, often with the sense of having put everything into it. Common in talk about work, training, and personal goals.

examples.japanese: {最後|さいご}までやり{切|き}った。
examples.english: I saw it through to the end.

examples.japanese: {決|き}めたことはやり{切|き}りたい。
examples.english: I want to carry through whatever I have decided to do.

examples.japanese: {難|むずか}しい{仕事|しごと}だったが、チーム{全員|ぜんいん}でやり{切|き}ることができた。
examples.english: It was a difficult job, but the whole team managed to see it through.

notes:
Formed from やる (to do) plus the auxiliary {切|き}る, which adds the sense of doing something completely or to the limit — as in {使|つか}い{切|き}る (to use up) and {出|だ}し{切|き}る (to give everything one has).

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive; the thing completed is marked with を, though it is often left unstated when clear from context ({最後|さいご}までやり{切|き}る).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最後|さいご}までやり{切|き}る: to see it through to the very end
- {自分|じぶん}で{決|き}めたことをやり{切|き}る: to follow through on one's own decisions
- やり{切|き}る{力|ちから}: the ability to follow through

SIMILAR WORDS:
- やり{遂|と}げる: to accomplish — more formal and literary, stressing achievement of a goal
- {済|す}ませる: to get done — neutral about effort; simply finishing a task
